claims.claim: Cyril of Alexandria was Patriarch of Alexandria from 412 to 444.
Cyril was born circa 375-376 and died on June 27, 444.
Theodore of Mopsuestia was bishop of Mopsuestia in Cilicia for about 36 years and died in 428.

Theodore was a pupil of Diodore and his early controversy against Arians and Apollinarians led him to speak of the Incarnation as though it were only a condescension of God the Son connecting with Himself a man who had an already distinct being.
The fragments of Book 3 were translated by P. E. Pusey and published in LFC 47 (1881) on pages 350-362.

The fragments are grouped with Cyril's other anti-Nestorian and anti-Antiochene works including Five Tomes Against Nestorius, Scholia on the Incarnation, Christ Is One, and fragments against Diodore of Tarsus and the Synousiasts.
Cyril was named a doctor of the church in 1882.
